body: Please post the output of `STARSHIP_LOG=trace starship module nodejs` when the version does not show.

> STARSHIP_LOG=trace starship module nodejs

OK, I will continue to follow up. Once there is any progress, I will update it here.

I will note that I've seen behavior like this on supercompute nodes where the program binary is stored somewhere else (in my case, `julia` is stored on the networked Lustre FS). When initially trying to execute the command, it times out. Once you execute the command manually, it gets loaded into the OS cache and can execute under the timeout.

You would usually expect to see timeout warnings when this is happening, however, so I don't think it's exactly the same issue here.

@chipbuster 
> You would usually expect to see timeout warnings when this is happening, however, so I don't think it's exactly the same issue here.

I'm sorry, I forgot to mention. I did get the following hint.
> Executing command "/Users/user/n/bin/node" timed out. You can set command_timeout in your config to a higher value to allow longer-running commands to keep executing.

@liby If a command times out, the version not showing up is expected, because the version command fails to finish on time. If you want to allow for the command to execute for a longer time, you can increase the `command_timeout` to for instance 1 second with `starship config command_timeout 1000`.

Executing `node` likely just ensures that the binary is cached in memory and thus finishes executing faster. For possible improvements, you can follow #2543.
